newsitem.title: USA: More European insurers named in Holocaust suit.
newsitem.headline: More European insurers named in Holocaust suit.

text.p: Several major European insurers have been added to a complaint filed earlier this year by Holocaust victims and their families, bringing the total number of insurers involved to 16, according to court papers.

The amended complaint, filed late last month, broadens the the suit to include additional big-name insurers such as France's Union des Assurances de Paris and Switzerland's Winterthur Insurance Co and Zurich Insurance Co's Zurich Life Insurance Co.
Other European insurers may still be named in the lawsuit as attorneys unravel the connections between the old insurance policies and current insurers, a plaintiffs' attorney said.
"There are a number of companies that we're still investigating," said Linda Gerstel, a plaintiff attorney with the New York law firm of Anderson Kill & Olick.
However, two insurers named in the original lawsuit have been dropped from the complaint.
The original suit, which was filed in Manhattan federal court in March, seeks class action certification.
The proposed class consists of individuals who between 1920 and 1945 bought life, property and casualty insurance policies and annuities from the defendants.
The suit estimates that the class would exceed 10,000 members and seeks billions of dollars in damages to be determined at trial.
According to the suit, members of the class who were unable to flee the Nazi persecution were arrested and their assets, including the insurance policies, were taken by the Nazis.
The policies were then improperly transferred, liquidated or cashed in, the suit alleged.
"In many instances proceeds from the insurance policies of Holocaust victims were used to finance and extend the war or enrich Nazi war criminals," the plaintiffs alleged.

However, many of the insurance companies that sold the Holocaust victims these policies have since merged with other insurers, making it difficult to determine who is responsible for the liability, Gerstel said.
"We have to, with respect to some plaintiffs, still figure out the lines of liability that might flow through to some present day companies," she said.
In addition, she said, "we still get plaintiffs calling us up pointing to other companies; the investigation still continues."
A conference with U.S. District Judge Michael Mukasey is scheduled for August 20.
Most of the new companies added to the suit are from Germany, including Victoria Life Insurance Co, a unit of Victoria Holding AG.
Munich Re last week agreed to buy Victoria Holding in a deal that will make it the second largest insurer in Germany behind Allianz AG Holding.

Other new companies named include Gerling Konzern Life Insurance Co, Nordstern Life Insurance Co, Vereinte Insurance Co, Mannheimer Life Insurance Co and Deutscher Ring Life Insurance Co, all of Germany.
Basler Life Insurance Co, Winterthur and Zurich, all of Switzerland, Adriavita SpA of Italy and UAP of France also have been added to the suit.
Previously named were Assicurazioni Generali SpA of Italy, Wiener Allianz Insurance Co of Vienna, Riunione Adriatica Di Sicurta of Milan; Allianz of Germany and Der Anker Allgemeine of Vienna.
A.G.F. Assurances Generales de France Vie of Paris and Bavarian Reinsurance Co of Munich have been dropped from the action.
